div.academic: When the project involves fictional worlds, serious research, or content that needs real grounding.
div.design: When you need to improve how the app looks, how usable it is, or the overall user experience.
div.engineering: When you need to build, fix, or improve the project's code and infrastructure.
div.finance: When you need to make sense of numbers, pricing, budgets, or the business's financial health.
div.game-development: When the project is a game or has game elements.
div.gis: When the project involves maps, geographic data, or location.
div.healthcare: When the project is in healthcare and needs to follow industry rules.
div.marketing: When you need to attract, engage, or retain users with content.
div.paid-media: When you're paying for ads and want to improve the return on every dollar spent.
div.product: When you need to decide WHAT to build and in what order.
div.project-management: When you need to organize tasks, deadlines, and the team's workflow.
div.research: When you need to separate fact from opinion in research and sources.
div.sales: When you need to sell, prospect for customers, or look after existing ones.
div.security: Before launch and whenever user data is involved — it's the project's life insurance.
div.spatial-computing: When the project involves augmented/virtual reality or advanced 3D.
div.specialized: Special roles for specific situations — come here when you face an unusual challenge.
div.support: When you need to care for customers after launch or organize day-to-day operations.
div.testing: Before declaring anything “done” — this is where the proof that it works lives.

custom.code-reviewer: After any major code change. Say: “use the code-reviewer to review change X with a focus on correctness and security”.
custom.devops-automator: When it's time to set up the deploy, the CI/CD, and publish the platform (e.g., deploy on Zorin/Docker).
custom.reality-checker: Before believing anything is done. Say: “verify with evidence that X actually works”. It accepts no promises, only proof.
custom.api-tester: To test the backend routes end to end (login, matches, invites, rankings, payments).
custom.test-automation-engineer: To create the automated test suite that runs on its own with every change (Playwright/Cypress).
custom.evidence-collector: To turn “I tested it and it works” into a report with reproducible proof — and honestly mark what wasn't tested.
custom.accessibility-auditor: Before public launch: makes sure the app works for everyone (keyboard, screen readers, contrast).
custom.performance-benchmarker: When the app is slow or before launch, to measure and improve speed with hard numbers.
custom.penetration-tester: MANDATORY before opening to the public: simulates real attacks to find gaps before criminals do.
custom.application-security-engineer: To review the security of new code: exposed secrets, permissions, injection flaws.
custom.threat-detection-engineer: After launch: sets up the monitoring and alerts that detect attacks in production.
custom.sprint-prioritizer: At the start of each cycle: turns “everything is urgent” into an ordered plan with a clear first milestone.
